story time (night time edition)
From: Natalie Miesak <4804135947@students.ocps.net>
To: Brandon Nova <4804241180@students.ocps.net>, Gianna Kim <4804135863@students.ocps.net>, Lauren Willman <4804089800@students.ocps.net>, Olivia Yip <4804085190@students.ocps.net>, Tyler Szydlo <4804136151@students.ocps.net>
Date: Thu, 18 Jan 2024 05:51:19 -0500
Labels: Archived, Important, Opened, Category Personal, MEMORIES ARCHIVE
Message-ID: <CAGZ_XgCr-W+mn93B-x5i-WRB-z53bCKrOEGdKtucfRFELK+7tA@mail.gmail.com>

The silence is hauntingly peaceful. Darkness cloaks him like a warm
blanket. Tyler is sitting in his house at 3 am, studying intently on how to
perfectly fold a hoodie. Dozens of tabs open, running 2 videos at the same
time, reading articles, Tyler is working so hard to master this craft.

 EERRRREEEECCCHH!

 Tyler looks up and surveys the room. Where did that sound come from? Oh
well. Maybe he’s stayed up too late and is hallucinating. Whatever- he must
continue his studies. Tyler pulls up another video on how to fold hoodies.


“I wouldn’t do that if I were you.”

 Tyler looks around again. Who said that? Where did it come from? The voice
sounds eerily like Lauren, but Lauren is nowhere to be seen. Just then, a
floating hoodie drifts into the room.

 “You can’t learn how to fold hoodies. They deserve to be free, not
constricted as so!” said the hoodie.
“Lauren, is that you?” questioned Tyler.
“Yes. I have been trapped inside this hoodie. You have to save me!”

 Tyler feels a sudden sense of urgency. He must save Lauren from the
clutches of the hoodie! He knows just where to start. Tyler opens his
window and jumps out, running towards the lake.

 The cold air brushes past his face as he runs faster and faster towards
the lake. But he is suddenly stopped by Gianna. She has a look of pure
horror on her face.
“You can’t go there! I’ve already tried to save Lauren. There is no point”
exclaimed Gianna. Tyler, confused, tries to figure out why. Gianna swiftly
turns into a hat. This is not good.

 Tyler is determined to save the day, so he continues towards the Lake.
Finally he makes it to the lake, and feels the cool mist blowing against
his face. In the middle of the lake sits Olivia, floating and meditating
over the surface of the water. She warns Tyler not to come any closer, but
Tyler has to save his friends.
“Turn them back into people!” demanded Tyler. “no” proclaimed Olivia very
seriously.

 Tyler begins running on the water. He will do whatever it takes to stop
this madness. Suddenly, Olivia pulls out a magic wand and points it at
Tyler. He realizes too late that he is her next target.

 “NOOOOOOO!” Brandon flies across the water, blocking the hit from the
magic wand.
“Brandon, you sacrificed yourself for me?” asked Tyler. Brandon lies on the
surface of the water, barely breathing.
“I know you would do the same for me” replied Brandon very dramatically.
 “No Brandon! Stay with me!”

 Brandon swiftly transforms into a pair of shoes. Before Tyler can fully
register the weight of this sacrifice, Olivia points the wand at him again.
Tyler, still in shock, has no time to react. He faces the magic of her
wand, and is turned into a beautiful dress. Olivia has won again.

The end.

story time (desert edition)
From: Natalie Miesak <4804135947@students.ocps.net>
To: Brandon Nova <4804241180@students.ocps.net>, Tyler Szydlo <4804136151@students.ocps.net>, Olivia Yip <4804085190@students.ocps.net>, Lauren Willman <4804089800@students.ocps.net>, Gianna Kim <4804135863@students.ocps.net>
Date: Wed, 17 Jan 2024 11:34:35 -0500
Labels: Archived, Important, Opened, Category Personal, Important Inforation
Message-ID: <CAGZ_XgAOMKRPNeG77mEJh3i3JVuoUP2+UOcRKbCm0e+FQWLVqw@mail.gmail.com>

The sun's intense heat is unrelenting. Brandon slowly treks through the
endless sandy landscape. He's been stranded in the desert for 23 years,
with no food and no water. He still struggles to find his way out of the
desert, knowing that someday he will find civilization again. The sun
shines directly overhead, and Brandon realizes that it's lunchtime. He
picks up some sand and uses his brainpower to shape the sand into a basket
of french fries. He snacks on his sand fries as he continues to walk
through the desert.

Just then, he hears the sound of a galloping horse. He turns to realize
that it wasn't a horse, but a giant sea turtle. *That must mean there's
water nearby!* Brandon thought to himself. But the sea turtle turned into
Tyler.
"I can help!" said Tyler.
"Great!" said Brandon. "I need to get out of this desert."
Tyler, understanding Brandon's request perfectly, swiftly turned into a
boat.

Brandon, now eternally grateful to Tyler, begins hauling the boat through
the desert. He moves at a swift 0.004 m/s as he drags the boat through the
sand.

Just then, he hears the sound of a galloping horse. He turns to realize
that it was a horse! On the horse rides Lauren and Gianna. Lauren
approaches Brandon and his boat.
"Oh lovely! We actually need a boat. Would you like to trade?" exclaimed
Lauren. "I'll give you my horse as compensation."

Brandon thinks about the offer, but decides to decline. He doesn't need a
horse. He is perfectly fine with his boat. But Olivia miraculously slips
out of Lauren's pocket and faces Brandon.
"No, we need this boat. You have to give it to us," demanded Olivia very
politely.

Brandon thinks for a few hours, and he agrees to trade. Lauren, Olivia, and
Gianna get back in the boat and zip off into the distance at a whopping 332
m/s.

Brandon looks back at his horse. *What am I supposed to do with this?* he
thinks to himself. Brandon then remembers that he is very hungry. The horse
would be a perfect source of food! Brandon begins building a sand mound so
he can start a sand fire. Just then, the horse turns into Tyler.
"No! You can't kill me!" proclaims Tyler.

Brandon can't argue with that. He decides to make another batch of sand
fries, and shares some with Tyler. The sun is beginning to set, the air
already getting cooler. They finish their fries, and begin walking into the
distance. Brandon is still stuck in the desert, but now he has someone to
share the journey with him.

Tyler turns into a bird and flies away. The end.

Re: story time
From: Brandon Nova <4804241180@students.ocps.net>
To: Natalie Miesak <4804135947@students.ocps.net>
Cc: Lauren Willman <4804089800@students.ocps.net>, Olivia Yip <4804085190@students.ocps.net>, Gianna Kim <4804135863@students.ocps.net>, Tyler Szydlo <4804136151@students.ocps.net>
Date: Tue, 16 Jan 2024 14:50:43 -0500
Labels: Archived, Sent, Opened, MEMORIES ARCHIVE
Message-ID: <CANuu65HTQ8rw8_izVmEfW3YMasUn-yDO_S6PJXhthk4HPVP-bQ@mail.gmail.com>

Lauren's urgent quest through the forest, the stone building, and the
guarded entrance are representative of her subconscious. The rain and
running symbolizes urgency or emotional turmoil. The bridge across the moat
signifies a transition or challenge that she must overcome and the guards
are people encountered on those challenges.

Brandon, the serious guard, and Olivia, the mean guard, could represent
different aspects of Lauren's psyche. Brandon, perhaps, symbolizes a
compliant, weak, rational, rule-based part of her mind, while Olivia might
represent a harsh, realistic, and critical inner voice.

The snake that transforms into Tyler may be a symbol of transformation or a
hidden aspect of Lauren's desires. The chase through the hallways and
twisting and turning reflects the complexities of her inner thoughts and
conflicts.

The basement and prison cells could symbolize repressed emotions or
memories that Lauren needs to confront. Gianna, practicing Japanese
peacefully, might represent a harmonious and creative aspect of Lauren's
psyche that is imprisoned or overlooked, as Gianna is literally imprisoned.

Natalie, imprisoned with the key, could represent a part of Lauren's psyche
holding the solution to her struggles. The use of the power of friendship
to trap Olivia might suggest that interpersonal relationships and support
play a crucial role in overcoming inner conflicts.

Ultimately, Lauren and Gianna leaving the prison together and living
happily ever after could signify a resolution or integration of different

The rain is coming down in buckets. Lauren is running as hard as she can
through the forest. The wind rushes past her ears, barely covered by the
hood of her black cloak. She urges herself to run faster, never allowing
herself to stop. *I have to save them*, she thinks to herself. She is
nearly blinded by the rain as she continues her sprint through the forest,
dodging bushes and side-stepping tree branches,

She comes to a stop behind a tree, and allows herself to catch her breath.
Not more than 30 meters away stands a towering building made of solid stone
bricks, no windows, no doors. The only way to enter is to get across the
bridge spanning a large moat, through the front gate which is guarded by a
very serious guard (aka Brandon). Lauren calms herself and approaches the
guard.
"Halt! State your business here," says Brandon.
"I come on very important business matters," Lauren replies, very
seriously.
Brandon thinks for a few hours. "Very well." Brandon opens the gate, and
Lauren enters very swiftly.

She walks through stone hallways lit with torches. She looks around for the
staircase to the basement, when she sees the mean guard (aka Olivia)
walking on the far end of the hallway.
"STOP!" proclaims Olivia.
Lauren turns the other direction and runs. She twists through the hallways,
not knowing where to go. She has to get away from Olivia, but she has to
find that staircase. A snake slithers out of a hole in the floor and blocks
her path. The snake then transforms into Tyler.
"Follow me!" yells Tyler.

They proceed to run through the hallways, and finally arrive at the
staircase. Tyler turns back into a snake and slithers away. Lauren quickly
makes her way down the stairs. At the bottom, there is a long hallway lined
with prison cells. Lauren runs through the cells, anxious to find Gianna.
She must save her from the evil clutches of Olivia. Lauren finally comes to
a stop and sees Gianna peacefully practicing her Japanese.

Lauren frantically searches for a way to unlock the cell door. She hears a
voice from the opposite side of the hallway.
"I can help. I have the key to all the cells. You just need to let me out."
says Natalie.
Lauren turns to see Natalie is also imprisoned inside a jail cell.
"You need to give me the keys to Gianna's cell first" Lauren says.
Natalie agrees, and gives Lauren the key. Lauren unlocks Gianna's cell.
Just then, Olivia is heard walking down the stairs. They have to go. Lauren
opens the door and lets Gianna out, and makes a silent promise to never
return and save Natalie.

Lauren and Gianna quickly leave the hallway, looking for an alternate way
out. But there is no other way out. They go to the stairs, where Olivia is
standing ominously. Lauren uses the power of friendship to defeat Olivia,
and Olivia is magically trapped in Gianna's old cell. Lauren and Gianna
make their way out of the prison.

"Hey! What are you doing?" questions Brandon, who is still guarding the
gate.
"I'm leaving" replies Lauren.

Brandon does not question this. Lauren and Gianna walk out of the prison
like girlbosses, and live happily ever after.

The end.

Why you do you think those adjectives above describe you? *
I like talking to people. I'm a people person. I spend a lot of time
talking to people. I also try to help people a lot. I tutor, and sometimes
teach. When people ask me for help I try to explain the concept behind it.
When people tell me their problems I listen. I do this because I can. I

What is your planned major or area of interest? *
Psychology or Business
What led you to pursue this major? (If there is a story about how you
landed on this major or someone who impacted your life that helped you make
this decision, please tell us!) *
I started trying to change myself (its futile to change others, not that I
tried that, I didn't) and I love learning about things I can apply. After
taking psychology with Hannigan I really saw the impact the field could
have. Also I love talking to people.
What are the reasons that you chose the schools you are currently applying
to? Please also list them here. *
I believe that if I go to Stanford I can change the world or something.
It's a little lottery I will play and allow God to decide my fate. I'm not
extremely religious though I believe in Christ as my savior and that he
died for me. I want to be able to make an impact on others, to allow them
to enable themselves. Most people feel stuck. I can feel it. They feel
stuck, or they get themselves caught up in something, to turn something
else into their life. I want to allow people to have the option to free
themselves. August 1981, Stanford Psychology hall. They never talk about
their life outside. Why is that? Nothing stops them. Nothing. They could.
We could. We don't. What stops us, really? I want to go to Stanford. UPenn
is so I can network with people and become wealthy, though there's
definitely other paths to that.
What subjects are you most interested in for school? *
Last year I loved psychology. I never did anything for the class, but I
payed attention raptly everyday. I could watch Hannigan all day. She was so
engaging. I was so excited to enter her class. She would tell vivid
stories, scenarios, or past episodes. I always remembered everything. This
year I'm interested in Physics and Literature. I don't pay attention in
physics, but I know enough to have invented my own pseudoscience. I'm
getting a bunch of people together to work on it, but I need knowledge of
mechanical physics to unlock the human mind. It's complicated. I can't do
arithmetic, yet. I took physics to unlock the secrets of the universe, but
we're learning about things being suspended from pulleys, and falling
blocks on slopes, which is nice. In Literature Mr. Cary imparts his
infinite wisdom on us. He just gets life. Seize the day, live for the
moment, be happy. I strive to achieve that level of fulfillment in life.
Though he definitely helps us get there. It makes me feel good to think of
how many lives he has changed for the better, and how many more yet to
come.
Have you had any major life experiences that you would like to be noted in
your letter (for example, moving here from another country or volunteering
at Give Kids The World helped you realize you want to do cancer research,
etc) *
I had a walk, with my friend, in September, many years ago (2021). He said
how he had learned philosophy and applied it in his life. It clicked that I
could be anyone I wanted. That was definitely a turning point in my life. I
began reading and writing a lot. I gained a lot of knowledge. I grew as a
person. I definitely forced myself into more of a person I wanted to be. I
didn't discover some massive insight, I just realized I could be me, and
that me could be anyone I wanted it to be.
Does you academic record reflect an accurate record of your abilities? It
not, what should a college admissions officer consider as the best measure
of your academic potential? Is yes, how have your worked up to your
potential in high school? Please list if you feel COVID impacted your
education. *
My academic record is a horrible reflection of my abilities. I know how
easy it is to do 8 APs in a school year on top of 10 dual enrollments. With
self induced trance, inception, subconscious outsourcing (it's from a
trippy book, but it works), and time management I was able to do all of it
while still spending a lot of time talking with family and hanging out with
friends. I do acknowledge I have the privledge of not needing to work a job
to support my family, which gave me a lot of extra time. I use a white
board and notebook to keep track, and I break down what I need to do each
day. My academic record looks really bad because I was homeschooled, and
now it looks like I have bad grades (when I was literally never doing
school and spent my time on Salesforce and grand strategy games). COVID
didn't impact me, since I was already homeschooled. I feel the best measure
of my academic potential is the thousands of pages of personal works I have
personally written in the fields of social psychology, economics, and
philosophy. These works demonstrate the level of time I spent reading,
learning, and growing as a person as well as how I am able to combine these
ideas into a coherent flow I use to keep my life under control.
What has been one of your most stimulating or intellectual experiences? (If
you cannot think of any, simply write "unknown" *
One of my most intellectual experiences is my development of the field of
Psyphysics (Psychological physics) of which I am its inventor. After taking
AP Physics 1, AP Physics C: Mechanics, and Physics with Calculus (at
community college) combined with a passion for social psychology that led
dozens of my pens gone to fill thousands of pages, I decided to merge the
fields of Psychology and Physics. After having a mental trip at 4am (when I
sometimes wake up to dance) I started applying the laws of physics to the
mind, and started mapping out functions to relate all the forces to real
world forces. Since me and a lot of my friends got 5s in Calculus BC as
juniors, I worked with them to further this field. This is my commitment
now, to figure out a formulaic approach to the complexes of the human mind.
Using kinematics equations to map thoughts, and "traversing the road", as
our team motto states. We now work to further integrate mechanical physics
into our field, as well as traversing roadblocks we hit, such as "Tyler's
paradox" in which functions can cancel out to zero (although we use
L'hopital's from Calculus to overcome this). Creating the field of
Psyphysics and advancing it with my friends (who are the smartest people in
my school) has enabled me to push the limits of our minds to discover how
to unlock the mind.

2023-2024 Windermere High Parking Privilege: Pre-Registration Form

The staff of Windermere High are excited to start a new school year with  
you! Please read the information contained here entirely and then complete  
the required information to begin the process of obtaining a Parking Space  
for the 2023-2024 school year. Please note that parking spots are only sold  
to seniors and juniors. Sophomores can only purchase a parking spot if they  
meet the requirements AND are dual enrollment. Freshman can not purchase a  
parking spot.



This school year, students will be given the chance to purchase a Parking  
Space based on grade level, GPA, discipline, and attendance.  
Pre-Registration will be done very similar to the way that Prom and  
Homecoming were done for this past school year.



If you have any questions or concerns, you can reach out to one of the  
Discipline Clerks, Mia Sarnes at mialuisa.sarnes@ocps.net or Katherine  
Condron at katherine.condron@ocps.net



Process for Obtaining a Parking Space:



Complete this form
If cleared, you will be sent a link to purchase your space
However, you will not be enabled to purchase a ticket until the correlating  
sale date based off of grade, GPA, discipline, and attendance (broken down  
in the next section). You will be able to access the link to purchase, but  
your name/Student ID will not work until your designated purchasing window
If you are not cleared, you will receive a notification email. If there are  
any spots remaining, you will be notified.
When you come pick up your parking hanger, you will need to bring the  
signed WHS 23-24 Parking Agreement form in order to receive your hanger  
(form found here: https://tinyurl.com/WHSParkAgreement2324 ). Copies will  
be available at the school, but will still need to be signed by the student  
and their guardian.

You need to upload the following documents to this form (must be readable):


Driver's License
Copy of Insurance policy w/ student listed as insured
Valid Vehicle Registration

This process was created in order to alleviate lines and waits while still  
adhering to required/mandated school policies and procedures. Again, once  
the student has been checked and verified, a link to purchase 1 parking  
space will be sent to that student via their OCPS student email.


Your email (4804241180@students.ocps.net) was recorded when you submitted  
this form.

4804241180@students.ocps.net


2023-2024 Windermere High Parking: Overall Standing

Like mentioned before, Parking Spots will be sold based off of grade, GPA,  
discipline, and attendance. Based on your overall standing, you will be  
assigned a day that you can purchase your pass using the link that is sent  
to you once you're cleared. Unlike Prom and Homecoming, there is no "10  
days of perfect attendance" to make up attendance issues. Please take note  
that 5 unexcused absences from individual classes equals 1 unexcused school  
day. The standards are broken down below:



Discipline (applies to everyone): No level 3 or 4 referrals from the  
2022-2023 school year



FIRST RUN - PURCHASE DATE 6/19 (SENIORS ONLY)



2.5 GPA or above
less than 15 unexcused absences from the 2nd semester
less than 20 tardies from the 2nd semester


SECOND RUN - PURCHASE DATE 6/20 (JUNIORS ONLY)



2.5 GPA or above
less than 15 unexcused absences from the 2nd semester
less than 20 tardies from the 2nd semester


THIRD RUN - PURCHASE DATE 6/21 (SENIORS AND JUNIORS)


2.0 GPA or above
less than 20 unexcused absences from the 2nd semester
less than 30 tardies from the 2nd semester

FOURTH RUN - PURCHASE DATE 6/22



Sophomores who are in DUAL ENROLLMENT that meet the requirements of the  
FIRST RUN

in academics, discipline, and attendance. *

2023-2024 Windermere High Parking: New Purchase Procedures

This year, instead of students paying $100 up front for the entire school  
year, students will now have 2 payments of $50, one for the first semester,  
and then if approved, $50 for the second semester.



This allows WHS to ensure that students are meeting the academic,  
attendance, and discipline requirements to have the privilege to park on  
campus and to open up spots for those who were unable to secure a spot  
during the first semester. Students who do not meet the requirements at the  
end of the first semester will have their parking hanger and parking  
privileges revoked for the second semester. Below is the new procedures  
broken down step by step:



Before the 23-24 school year starts: Students who are approved for first  
semester parking will pay $50.
At the end of the first semester: Students who already park on campus and  
still meet attendance/academic/discipline standards will get the chance  
to "renew" their parking spot for the second semester for another $50.  
Students who do not meet these standards (and their parents) will get an  
email stating that their parking privileges are revoked for the second  
semester due to not meeting these standards. These students will not be  
able to park on campus starting the beginning of the second semester



Renewal Requirements: 2.0 GPA, less than 15 full-day absences (missing  
individual classes count towards this total as well), less than 20 tardies,  
no level 3 or 4 referrals
Individual Class Absences: the number of absences equivalent to a student  
missing half a day of school will equal 1 unexcused full-day absence, per  
OCPS attendance standards

Example: For a student who has 7 classes on campus, 4 unexcused class  
absences will equal 1 full day unexcused absence. For a student who only  
has 4 classes on campus, 2 unexcused class absences equal 1 unexcused  
full-day absence.



Beginning of the second semester: Students who are on the WHS Parking  
Waiting List AND meet academic/attendance standards will be offered a  
parking spot for the second semester for $50 if spaces become available.

Attendance Requirements include, but are not limited to: excessive  
tardiness or absenteeism, considered truant per OCPS guidelines, and  
unauthorized absences from class



Academic Requirements include, but are not limited to: GPA and failing  
classes from the first semester, especially if connected to attendance  
issues



Discipline Requirements include, but are not limited to: receiving level 3  
or 4 referrals

changed this year from $100 at the beginning of the year to $50 per  
semester. You understand that you can get your parking pass revoked for the  
second semester if you do not meet academic, discipline, and attendance  
requirements.

Does you academic record reflect an accurate record of your abilities? It  
not, what should a college admissions officer consider as the best measure  
of your academic potential? Is yes, how have your worked up to your

My academic record is a horrible reflection of my abilities. I know how  
easy it is to do 8 APs in a school year on top of 10 dual enrollments. With  
self induced trance, inception, subconscious outsourcing (it's from a  
trippy book, but it works), and time management I was able to do all of it  
while still spending a lot of time talking with family and hanging out with  
friends. I do acknowledge I have the privledge of not needing to work a job  
to support my family, which gave me a lot of extra time. I use a white  
board and notebook to keep track, and I break down what I need to do each  
day. My academic record looks really bad because I was homeschooled, and  
now it looks like I have bad grades (when I was literally never doing  
school and spent my time on Salesforce and grand strategy games). COVID  
didn't impact me, since I was already homeschooled. I feel the best measure  
of my academic potential is the thousands of pages of personal works I have  
personally written in the fields of social psychology, economics, and  
philosophy. These works demonstrate the level of time I spent reading,  
learning, and growing as a person as well as how I am able to combine these  
ideas into a coherent flow I use to keep my life under control.


What has been one of your most stimulating or intellectual experiences? (If  
you cannot think of any, simply write "unknown" *


One of my most intellectual experiences is my development of the field of  
Psyphysics (Psychological physics) of which I am its inventor. After taking  
AP Physics 1, AP Physics C: Mechanics, and Physics with Calculus (at  
community college) combined with a passion for social psychology that led  
dozens of my pens gone to fill thousands of pages, I decided to merge the  
fields of Psychology and Physics. After having a mental trip at 4am (when I  
sometimes wake up to dance) I started applying the laws of physics to the  
mind, and started mapping out functions to relate all the forces to real  
world forces. Since me and a lot of my friends got 5s in Calculus BC as  
juniors, I worked with them to further this field. This is my commitment  
now, to figure out a formulaic approach to the complexes of the human mind.  
Using kinematics equations to map thoughts, and "traversing the road", as  
our team motto states. We now work to further integrate mechanical physics  
into our field, as well as traversing roadblocks we hit, such as "Tyler's  
paradox" in which functions can cancel out to zero (although we use  
L'hopital's from Calculus to overcome this). Creating the field of  
Psyphysics and advancing it with my friends (who are the smartest people in  
my school) has enabled me to push the limits of our minds to discover how  
to unlock the mind.

[https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/2-EynBPPafGTa-i0XmCSNEpq5I61AqevwE1Zs057-IPKnlq4ZD42GuQQS58XWdt4DiLClL6bGPtQrAFSNheQTltTrD2PTgyUpnS1IU3LosCmtxOJgICBY1bAVuZxr8SSQj5P_ZQ-Kj9E1oHc29MhHw]
You will use SCOIR to request transcripts. The only Florida schools who require transcripts are FIU and FGCU. All others only accept the SSAR/SPARK form for self-reported academic records. Your final transcripts will be sent through SCOIR, Skyward, or it will need to be picked up by you and mailed to the necessary schools.
Log into your SCOIR account by going to SCOIR<http://www.scoir.com/>
If you do not have a SCOIR account, you will sign up for one here: SCOIR - Get started with a free account<https://app.scoir.com/signup?hsid=100180>
You need to agree to both FERPA authorizations so we can send documents to the colleges you have chosen. Without these completed, your counselor cannot send your transcripts. We will not be sending transcripts, reports, or other documents through any other platform, including Common App.
Then, add all the colleges/universities to your "applying" list. Most of you have the schools listed in the "following" section and all you need to do is drag the schools into the applying list. Please keep this up to date so I know where you are applying.
This will prompt me to upload the necessary documents for each school (i.e. transcript, school reports and recommendation letters - if required).
Also, click on My Profile and go to Overview. Click the link to invite your parent(s). You can also add a secondary email account.
 After adding the colleges to your applying column, use the school checklist so you know what you need to send to colleges.
SCOIR is a very useful tool for searching for colleges. Please see this guide to help you understand how to search for other schools to apply to: How to Search Schools in SCOIR<https://windermerehs.ocps.net/UserFiles/Servers/Server_124933/File/Guidance/CollegeAdmissionPrep.pdf>
Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA)
Opens December 2023
You will need your parents' support to apply to FAFSA.  Start looking over the items needed now so you are ready to apply in December.
Beginning on after December 1st you are able to apply through this link FAFSA(r) Application | Federal Student Aid<https://studentaid.gov/h/apply-for-aid/fafsa>
Check out our FAFSA resources on Canvas in the Student Body page, then click Guidance
College & Career Specialist
Ms. Laurenzana can help!  She offers support for students who need help applying for college. Contact her at Nancy.Laurenzana@ocps.net<mailto:Nancy.Laurenzana@ocps.net> or make an appointment through bookings.
Recommendation Letters
Ongoing
Look at the requirements for the schools you are applying to. No Florida Public schools require a letter of recommendation except for Florida Polytechnic University and Florida International University. If a letter of rec is required, please complete the following form when requesting a recommendation letter
https://tinyurl.com/WHSLOR

SAT
Ongoing
To register for future dates and to send your scores here is the link: SAT Registration<https://collegereadiness.collegeboard.org/sat/register>
ACT
Ongoing
To register for future dates and to send your scores here is the link: ACT Registration<http://www.act.org/content/act/en/products-and-services/the-act/registration.html>
Sending SAT/ACT scores
You will need to send your scores to colleges you are applying to.  Log in to your College Board or ACT account and send the scores directly to the colleges you are applying to.  There is a small fee for sending scores.  This can take up to six weeks so start early!
SAT/ACT/College Waivers
Ongoing
Only students who qualify for Free/reduced lunch are eligible for fee waivers for SAT/ACT and College Apps. You will need to complete this form to determine eligibility: Household Economic Survey<https://www.ocps.net/departments/food_and_nutrition_services/parents>
You will receive an email with your status, which you will need to show your counselor to get a fee waiver. Fee Waiver for the SAT are added directly to your account.
Community Service
Ongoing
To submit community service or work hours please upload through the following link.  WHS Community Service<https://windermerehs.ocps.net/guidance/community_service>
Please note: It is your responsibility to check and make sure that your volunteer and work hours meet the guidelines provided by Bright Futures. Work hours and community service hours can now be combined.
Scholarships
Ongoing
Updated in SCOIR and through Canvas with Scholarship Saturday
Transcripts
Ongoing
You will add all schools that you are applying to in SCOIR for transcripts to be sent. If your school is not in SCOIR and a transcript needs to be physically mailed, your counselor will provide you with any information that will need to be mailed to them.
Bright Futures application
Opens: October 1st
Service Deadline: May
Test Deadline: August 31, 2024
We will assist all students with applying for Bright Futures in your English Classrooms, if you do not have English in a classroom, please apply and view these documents:

Bright Futures Student Handbook Bright Futures Student Handbook<https://www.floridastudentfinancialaidsg.org/PDF/BFHandbookChapter1.pdf>
Please complete to register and apply for Bright Futures
Florida Student Scholarship & Grant Programs<https://www.floridastudentfinancialaidsg.org/SAPBFMAIN/SAPBFMAIN>
Keep in mind that Bright Futures will not receive your test scores if you do not send them to a public university in the State of Florida. You can send them to the schools via your College Board/ACT account or by placing a Florida State University code inside of your answer sheet when you take the exam.
NCAA
Please be sure to look at the NCAA Eligibility Center if you are pursuing a scholarship. Notify your counselor by email if you are pursuing NCAA.
Register with the eligibility center and learn more at: NCAA.org<https://www.ncaa.org/>
College Applications
Varies - November 1, 2023 is the goal for all students.
College Application deadlines are approaching so start applying now:
You can apply to colleges/Universities through their website and you can also use the Common App to apply for more than 1 college at one time. The common app link is Common App<https://www.commonapp.org/>
**As a reminder, your counselor will not check common app for any colleges. All colleges you apply to must be updated in your SCOIR account. The Earlier you apply, the better! Many deadlines for complete applications (which means that the application, test scores, application fee paid, and SSAR/SPARK form complete) is due by November 1, 2023.
To view the State of Florida University System information (application deadlines, average scores), please visit this: SUS Matrix<https://drive.google.com/file/d/12T0JPVWL-AmkP9zbPObGDqbVZd3IS6b3/view?usp=sharing> (must be logged in to student email to view)

AP Macroecon LATE exam information
From: "Newcomer, Amanda H." <amanda.newcomer@ocps.net>
To: "4804241180@students.ocps.net" <4804241180@students.ocps.net>
Date: Tue, 16 May 2023 12:55:20 +0000
Labels: Archived, Important, Opened, Category Personal, College/AP
Message-ID: <SA1PR01MB7261D9018610E015A6D9FB1D86799@SA1PR01MB7261.prod.exchangelabs.com>

Dear Brandon Nova,
Listed below is part or all of your exam schedule. If you are taking multiple exams, you will receive multiple emails.  Please review each carefully for accuracy. If you see any discrepancies, please contact me immediately.
AP Exam
Date
Student Arrival Time
Room Number
AP Macroeconomics
Wednesday, May 17th
11:30:00 AM
Media Center

As a reminder, a parent or guardian MUST have completed the Google Form for you to leave campus after your morning exam.  If it has not been completed, you will return to class.
Below is information for the AP Exams for May 2023.  Please review ALL information carefully.
MOST afternoon AP exams end AFTER school ends (2:20).  Please ensure you have adequate transportation after your exam ends, as transportation is NOT provided.  You CANNOT be released from your exam early to ride a bus.
If you are testing in the GYM, we have found it to be VERY chilly as of late.  Please bring a jacket or sweatshirt to keep warm.
Before exam day:

  *   You will receive an email with your testing location.  Please check the location CAREFULLY.

*         You are required to arrive no later than 30 minutes prior to your exam: 7:30 a.m. for the morning administration and 11:30 a.m. for the afternoon administration. Students may not be dismissed until an exam has officially ended; do not ask to leave early if you finish before the end of the exam. If you play a sport or have a job, it is your responsibility to inform your coach or employer of your AP Exam obligation, and arrangements should be made accordingly.
Be sure to bring these:

  *   No. 2 pencils for your multiple-choice answer sheet.
  *   Pens with black or dark blue ink for completing areas on the exam booklet covers and for free-response questions in most exams.
  *   Up to two approved calculators with the necessary capabilities if you're taking an AP Biology, Calculus, Chemistry, Environmental Science, Macroeconomics, Microeconomics, Physics or Statistics Exam. Visit THIS LINK<https://apstudents.collegeboard.org/exam-policies-guidelines/calculator-policies> to learn more about the calculator policy for each of these exams and for a list of authorized calculators.
  *   A current government-issued or school-issued photo ID. (Additional ID may be required by authorized test centers outside the United States.)
     *   Windermere Students: your WHS ID is sufficient.  The one on your phone is fine, but your phone MUST be turned off immediately after your ID has been checked.
  *   Your College Board SSD Accommodations Letter if you are taking an exam with approved testing accommodations.
Don't bring these:

  *   Electronic equipment including phones, smartwatches, fitness trackers, wearable technology, cameras, recording or listening devices, or any other type of electronic or communication device.
     *   The only exceptions to the above restrictions are laptops or other devices specifically permitted to be used for in-school digital testing.
     *   School-owned and school-controlled digital recording devices are allowed only for the AP French, AP German, AP Italian, and AP Spanish Language and Culture Exams, and the AP Music Theory Exam.
  *   Books, reference guides, notes, compasses, protractors, mechanical pencils, pencils that are not No. 2, correction fluid, dictionaries, highlighters, or colored pencils.
  *   Scratch paper: Students testing in-school are prohibited from bringing scratch paper to the AP Exam, but scratch paper will be provided.
  *   Watches that beep, make a noise, or have an alarm.
  *   Computers or calculators that are not approved.
  *   Reference guides, keyboard maps, or other typing instructions.
  *   Ear plugs.
  *   Earbuds
  *   Clothing or shoes with subject-related information.
  *   Food or drink.
  *   Clipboards.
A student observed with any of these prohibited items during testing or breaks may be dismissed from the exam, the device may be confiscated, the student's score may be canceled, and no retest may be permitted.

Details about required and prohibited items are in the AP Exam Policies and Guidelines<https://apstudents.collegeboard.org/exam-policies-guidelines#sec1>.
Should you have any questions, please contact me directly.
Amanda Newcomer, M. Ed.
AP Coordinator
AICE Coordinator
Windermere High School
amanda.newcomer@ocps.net<mailto:amanda.newcomer@ocps.net>

  *   Electronic equipment including phones, smartwatches, fitness trackers, wearable technology, cameras, recording or listening devices, or any other type of electronic or communication device.
     *   The only exceptions to the above restrictions are laptops or other devices specifically permitted to be used for in-school digital testing.
     *   School-owned and school-controlled digital recording devices are allowed only for the AP French, AP German, AP Italian, and AP Spanish Language and Culture Exams, and the AP Music Theory Exam.
  *   Books, reference guides, notes, compasses, protractors, mechanical pencils, pencils that are not No. 2, correction fluid, dictionaries, highlighters, or colored pencils.
  *   Scratch paper: Students testing in-school are prohibited from bringing scratch paper to the AP Exam, but scratch paper will be provided.
  *   Watches that beep, make a noise, or have an alarm.
  *   Computers or calculators that are not approved.
  *   Reference guides, keyboard maps, or other typing instructions.
  *   Ear plugs.
  *   Earbuds
  *   Clothing or shoes with subject-related information.
  *   Food or drink.
  *   Clipboards.
A student observed with any of these prohibited items during testing or breaks may be dismissed from the exam, the device may be confiscated, the student's score may be canceled, and no retest may be permitted.

Details about required and prohibited items are in the AP Exam Policies and Guidelines<https://apstudents.collegeboard.org/exam-policies-guidelines#sec1>.
Should you have any questions, please contact me directly.
Amanda Newcomer, M. Ed.
AP Coordinator
AICE Coordinator
Windermere High School
amanda.newcomer@ocps.net<mailto:amanda.newcomer@ocps.net>

AP Exam
Date
Student Arrival Time
Room Number
AP Calculus BC
Monday, May 8th
7:30:00 AM
4-302

As a reminder, a parent or guardian MUST have completed the Google Form for you to leave campus after your morning exam.  If it has not been completed, you will return to class.
Below is information for the AP Exams for May 2023.  Please review ALL information carefully.
MOST afternoon AP exams end AFTER school ends (2:20).  Please ensure you have adequate transportation after your exam ends, as transportation is NOT provided.  You CANNOT be released from your exam early to ride a bus.
If you are testing in the GYM, we have found it to be VERY chilly as of late.  Please bring a jacket or sweatshirt to keep warm.
Before exam day:

  *   You will receive an email with your testing location.  Please check the location CAREFULLY.

*         You are required to arrive no later than 30 minutes prior to your exam: 7:30 a.m. for the morning administration and 11:30 a.m. for the afternoon administration. Students may not be dismissed until an exam has officially ended; do not ask to leave early if you finish before the end of the exam. If you play a sport or have a job, it is your responsibility to inform your coach or employer of your AP Exam obligation, and arrangements should be made accordingly.
Be sure to bring these:

  *   No. 2 pencils for your multiple-choice answer sheet.
  *   Pens with black or dark blue ink for completing areas on the exam booklet covers and for free-response questions in most exams.

Visit THIS LINK<https://apstudents.collegeboard.org/exam-policies-guidelines/calculator-policies> to learn more about the calculator policy for each of these exams and for a list of authorized calculators.
  *   A current government-issued or school-issued photo ID. (Additional ID may be required by authorized test centers outside the United States.)
     *   Windermere Students: your WHS ID is sufficient.  The one on your phone is fine, but your phone MUST be turned off immediately after your ID has been checked.

If you play a sport or have a job, it is your responsibility to inform your coach or employer of your AP Exam obligation, and arrangements should be made accordingly.
Be sure to bring these:

  *   No. 2 pencils for your multiple-choice answer sheet.
  *   Pens with black or dark blue ink for completing areas on the exam booklet covers and for free-response questions in most exams.
  *   Up to two approved calculators with the necessary capabilities if you're taking an AP Biology, Calculus, Chemistry, Environmental Science, Macroeconomics, Microeconomics, Physics or Statistics Exam. Visit THIS LINK<https://apstudents.collegeboard.org/exam-policies-guidelines/calculator-policies> to learn more about the calculator policy for each of these exams and for a list of authorized calculators.
  *   A current government-issued or school-issued photo ID. (Additional ID may be required by authorized test centers outside the United States.)
     *   Windermere Students: your WHS ID is sufficient.  The one on your phone is fine, but your phone MUST be turned off immediately after your ID has been checked.
  *   Your College Board SSD Accommodations Letter if you are taking an exam with approved testing accommodations.
Don't bring these:

  *   Electronic equipment including phones, smartwatches, fitness trackers, wearable technology, cameras, recording or listening devices, or any other type of electronic or communication device.
     *   The only exceptions to the above restrictions are laptops or other devices specifically permitted to be used for in-school digital testing.
     *   School-owned and school-controlled digital recording devices are allowed only for the AP French, AP German, AP Italian, and AP Spanish Language and Culture Exams, and the AP Music Theory Exam.
  *   Books, reference guides, notes, compasses, protractors, mechanical pencils, pencils that are not No. 2, correction fluid, dictionaries, highlighters, or colored pencils.
  *   Scratch paper: Students testing in-school are prohibited from bringing scratch paper to the AP Exam, but scratch paper will be provided.
  *   Watches that beep, make a noise, or have an alarm.
  *   Computers or calculators that are not approved.
  *   Reference guides, keyboard maps, or other typing instructions.
  *   Ear plugs.
  *   Earbuds
  *   Clothing or shoes with subject-related information.
  *   Food or drink.
  *   Clipboards.
A student observed with any of these prohibited items during testing or breaks may be dismissed from the exam, the device may be confiscated, the student's score may be canceled, and no retest may be permitted.

Details about required and prohibited items are in the AP Exam Policies and Guidelines<https://apstudents.collegeboard.org/exam-policies-guidelines#sec1>.
Should you have any questions, please contact me directly.

Good morning,

OCSP is offering a summer IT paid internship for a selected number of students.

  *   Each student must be 16 years old and have not graduated from High School. They will work 20 hours per week and be paid $16.00 per hour. we hope to have 100-150 students, placements will be determined by the Career specialist based on their recruitment and pre-interview of the students.
  *   All students will be required to provide their own transportation to and from their work assignment. We will work to ensure the student is placed as close to their home school as possible
  *   Students working at the ELC will go through a drug screen and background investigation at a cost of $92.50, which will be deducted over the six weeks of their employment.
  *   Placements in the following areas

     *   IT Summer refresh,  80-100+ Interns (all selected intern candidates will be interviewing with Omar Aponte Via Webex.
     *   ELC Reception Desk, 2 Interns (Will have to take part in PREO at the district level)
     *   ELC - Human Resources PREO, 3 Interns (Will have to take part in PREO at the district level)
     *   5 Students to work with District 2 Board Member - Maria Salamanca as part of a pilot program for a fellowship for students.  Board Member Salamanca represents Lake Nona High School and Colonial High School (Will have to take part in PREO at the district level)


If you would like to be considered for one of these positions please email me back so I can add your name to the District interest list.

If you have any questions you can email me or John De Rosa at   John.DeRosa@ocps.net

Dear Nova, Brandon,

The purpose of this Email is to inform you that you will take the computer-based Florida Civic Literacy Examination (FCLE) on 12/2/2022 in section C of the media center at 7:45 a.m. Make sure you report to your first period first then your teacher will excuse you to come to the media center.

In accordance with Florida Statutes<http://www.leg.state.fl.us/statutes/index.cfm?App_mode=Display_Statute&Search_String=1003.4282&URL=1000-1099/1003/Sections/1003.4282.html>, student taking a United States Government course are required to take the FCLE. Students who earn a passing score on the FCLE are exempt from the state's postsecondary civic literacy assessment requirement.

The FCLE is administered in one 160-minute session. Any student who has not completed the session by the end of the allotted time may continue working up to half the length of a typical school day.

If you would like to become familiar with the computer-based platform at home, you may access the FCLE practice test and answer key available at https://fsassessments.org/families.html.

Make sure you have a fully charged school computer!

For more information about the Florida Statewide Assessments program, please visit the portal at FLFAST.org<https://flfast.org/>.
